st_sommeil.name: Rue du Marchand-de-Sable
st_sommeil.alt: A cozy cobbled village lane on a warm summer evening, under a crescent moon and the first stars, with glowing lanterns, a tall iron lamp post, flower boxes and a ginger cat asleep on a cushion; three little cottages with a red door, a green door and a blue door. Monsieur Verbe climbs into a little bed under a patchwork quilt, hand mirror in hand; stretches his striped scarf longer and longer; checks his pocket watch by the lamp post in a purple beret; lifts a toppled lantern upright; and sits down on the bench in a gold beret, mirror in hand. The lane behind leads back to the Rue des Maisons.

levetot.name: Rue des Lève-tôt
levetot.alt: The back garden of a village cottage at sunrise, under a pink and gold sky, with a hammock between two trees, a bed with a patchwork quilt on the grass, a woodpile in shadow, a garden table and a black rooster crowing on the fence. Monsieur Verbe sleeps in the hammock in a gold beret; waves from the cottage window; sits up yawning in bed with his hand mirror; sits bored at the table, chin in hand, his mirror beside him; and sits mirror in hand in his buttoned brown coat. The red door leads back to the lane.

doors.label: Rue du Marchand-de-Sable
doors.hint: Back through the red cottage door

lavandieres.name: Allée des Lavandières
lavandieres.alt: A sunny cobbled wash-yard behind the cottages, with colorful sheets on the washing line, flower pots, a stone well and a sparkling window; a cottage with a green door on the left. Monsieur Verbe tidies his teddy, ball and blocks into a toy chest; bathes in a bubbly wooden tub with a rubber duck, mirror in hand; carries a tray of dirty cups and plates away; washes his hands in foaming water at the well, mirror in hand; carries the ladder away from the wall; and sponges the window until it sparkles.

doors.label: Rue du Marchand-de-Sable
doors.hint: Back through the green cottage door

brosses.name: Ruelle des Brosses
brosses.alt: A little cobbled courtyard of a cottage on a summer evening, with climbing roses, glowing lanterns, a big lit bay window and a blackboard on an easel; the cottage has a blue door. Monsieur Verbe wipes the chalk squiggles off the blackboard; brushes his hair with a big hairbrush, mirror in hand; ducks as a paper airplane whizzes past his nose; carries a strawberry cream cake in a green beret; carries a blue armchair toward the lit window; and shaves the foam off his chin, mirror in hand.
